# Coffee Consumption Group Project

## 1. Install The Libraries:

<!-- Check how to hide install notes and warnings -->


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel) 
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(plotly)
```
:::


## 2. Install The Data:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
coffee <- read.csv("../../../../data/coffee_survey.csv")
```
:::

Unfortunately this data is poorly formatted...

## 4. Prepare the data

#### Clean up the **favourites** column


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
coffee <- coffee %>% 
    mutate(favourite = str_replace_all(favourite, c(
      "Blended drink \\(e.g. Frappuccino\\)" = "Blended", 
      "Regular drip coffee" = "Drip")))   
```
:::


#### Clean up the **age** column


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
coffee <- coffee %>% 
    mutate(age = str_replace_all(age, c(
      " years old" = "", 
      ">65" = "65+")))  
```
:::


#### Clean up the **cups** column


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
coffee <- coffee %>% 
    mutate(cups = str_replace_all(cups, c(
      "More than 4" = "5+", 
      "Less than 1" = "<1")))  
```
:::


## 5. Visualise Coffee Preferences

### First let's see the distribution of favourite coffee types:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data = coffee,
           mapping = aes(y = favourite)) + 
      geom_bar()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r-intensives_Manoel_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


There's still a lot going on here... We can simplify the data by grouping coffee types into broader preperation styles.

### Group by **Preperation Style**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
 PrepStyle <- coffee %>% 
      mutate(prep = case_when(
        favourite %in% c("Mocha", "Latte", "Cappuccino", "Cortado", "Espresso")
        ~ "Espresso",
        favourite %in% c("Iced coffee", "Cold brew", "Blended") 
        ~ "Iced",
        favourite %in% c("Drip", "Pourover", "Americano") 
        ~ "Brewed",
        .default = "other"))
```
:::


### Now we can visualise these groups


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data = PrepStyle,
           mapping = aes(x = prep)) + 
      geom_bar()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r-intensives_Manoel_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


### Reorder Preperation Styles


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
PrepStyle$prep <- factor(PrepStyle$prep, levels=c(
  'other', 'Iced', 'Brewed', 'Espresso')
  )
```
:::


You can arrange the order of attributes to best visualise the data you are working with

### Stacked Bar Graphs

Now we can add **stacks** to the bar graphs to explore relationships between preperation and other attributes

#### Preperation by Age


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data = PrepStyle,
           mapping = aes(x=age, fill=prep)) + 
      geom_bar(position='stack') +
      geom_text(aes(label = after_stat(count)), 
                stat = "count", position = "dodge", check_overlap = TRUE
      )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r-intensives_Manoel_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data = PrepStyle,
      aes(fill=prep, x=age)) + 
  geom_bar(position='dodge') +
  geom_text(aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    stat = "count", position = position_dodge(.9)
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r-intensives_Manoel_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::
